COMMIT, REPORTED PLAINLY (rule 26), AND A LIMIT OF RULE 17 WORTH KNOWING. I committed with `git commit --only` over my three remaining declared paths (the other seven had already been swept into 79ff4c6 and 388f480 by orchestrator bank commits while I worked). The commit 402d01a nevertheless carries SEVEN files. Four of them — orchestration/INDEX.md, docs/index.html, docs/progress.html, docs/status.json — are staged by the pre-commit hook itself (`.githooks/pre-commit` lines 75 and 81 run `git add` on them unconditionally), so `--only` cannot exclude them; they are generated artifacts and the regeneration is derived from my own verdict and blog line. The fifth is reports/blog-feed.jsonl, which gained TWO lines rather than one: `--only` takes the whole file, and arbiter-dlg-s37 appended its line between my append and my commit. Nothing is lost — the file is append-only and that agent's line is intact — but it is committed under my message rather than theirs, and I am saying so rather than leaving it to be found. THE GENERAL POINT: `--only` restricts the commit to the paths you name, but it does not protect a shared APPEND-ONLY file from carrying a neighbour's interim write, and it does not override a hook that stages on your behalf. Rule 17 is right and is not sufficient on this tree.
